dataset_family: HABS-HD (Health & Aging Brain Study - Health Disparities): community-based multi-ethnic cohort (Mexican American, Black, non-Hispanic White) at the University of North Texas Health Science Center, Fort Worth, Texas; 2929 dementia-free participants
method_family: Cross-sectional biomarker epidemiology. Plasma AT(N) markers (SIMOA Abeta42/40, p-tau181, NfL) and 3T MRI FreeSurfer AD-signature cortical thickness, tested by linear regression on continuous GDS-30 and on high/low-symptom x MCI strata (adjusted marginal means, SMDs).
what_it_shows: Dintica, Johnson, Petersen, O'Bryant and Yaffe, Neurobiol Aging 158 (2026) 11-17. The PDF title, authors and DOI 10.1016/j.neurobiolaging.2025.11.005 match the block. Among 2929 dementia-free adults: (a) MCI was more common with high than with low GDS-30 symptoms (30.3% vs 19.3%, p < 0.001; unadjusted, Table 1). (b) In the whole mixed CU+MCI sample, a continuous GDS score (per 1 SD) was NOT associated with MRI AD-signature cortical thickness (beta -0.024, CI -0.062 to 0.014) or with plasma Abeta42/40. It WAS associated with plasma NfL (beta 0.008, CI 0.003-0.014) and p-tau181 (beta 0.074, CI 0.040-0.108). (c) In the four-stratum analysis, only the MCI + high-symptom group had thinner AD-signature cortex (SMD -0.30) and the largest p-tau181 excess (SMD 0.30), both relative to the cognitively normal low-symptom reference.
why: PARTLY. FIRST CLAUSE: shown. High depressive-symptom status goes with MCI (30.3% vs 19.3%). Caveats: the status is a GDS >= 10 symptom screen, not clinical depression, as the authors say themselves, and the comparison is unadjusted. SEVERITY CLAUSE: mixed. A continuous severity score failed to track the one structural brain measure (MRI AD-signature cortical thickness) and plasma amyloid, which is the kind of null the row describes. The same continuous score did track plasma NfL and p-tau181. If blood markers of neurodegeneration and tau count as MCI neurobiology, admitting P-720 would make the row's wording 'within the supporting studies, continuous severity scores fail to track brain measures' untrue, unless 'brain measures' is restricted to imaging. The paper fits the row's 'divided' framing but contradicts part of its supporter sentence. The categorical MCI + high-symptom stratum having thinner cortex is loosely analogous to P-643's categorical MDD-versus-STD FC difference (the row's 'although' clause), with three differences. The contrast is against a CU low-symptom reference, no within-MCI high-versus-low contrast is reported, and no MCI x symptom interaction is tested. The continuous-score analyses pool CU and MCI, so they are not tests within MCI. The design is cross-sectional, so the paper has nothing on conversion. The supplementary sensitivity analysis (GDS > 21) is described only in the text: 'no consistent associations' with Abeta42/40 or cortical thickness, and elevated p-tau181 and, to a lesser extent, NfL. REJECTION GROUND ANSWERED. P-720 was removed in the bulk G4 reverts of 2026-08-09 ('none of them makes the direct comparison this finding requires') and 2026-08-11 (severity must be tested against structural or functional brain measures). The PDF shows that it regresses continuous GDS-30 on 3T MRI cortical thickness, with a null result, so that generic ground does not hold for this paper. What limits it is the positive plasma associations and the pooled sample, not a missing comparison. DATA INCONSISTENCIES in the source: Table 1 group sizes (2430 + 569 = 2999) exceed the analysed 2929; the text says 644 had MCI (21.5%) while Table 1 gives 459 + 168 = 627; the Fig. 1 ns are 2373/554 and the Fig. 2 strata sum to 2927. The extract renders '=' as U+00BC in the Table 1 heading ('N ¼ 2430'). INDEPENDENCE. HABS-HD is distinct from P-643 (Korea University Guro), P-647 (Shanghai Brain Health Cohort), P-662 (Shanghai Tongji), P-663 (Florence) and the other candidates. Its MRI protocol is modelled on ADNI3, but the participants are not ADNI. No author is shared. The method family (plasma biomarker plus MRI regression) differs from P-647's; it overlaps P-643's imaging-correlation family only in the cortical-thickness test. Not a preprint.

quotes.quote: We cross-sectionally studied 2929 dementia-free participants from the Health & Aging Brain Study—Health Disparities (HABS-HD).

We measured depressive symptoms with the Geriatric Depression Scale 30-item (GDS) (Yesavage et al., 1982) a scale designed to be used for screening depression in older adults. Depressive symptoms were dichotomized as high (GDS≥10) versus low (GDS<10)
Participants with high depressive symptoms were more likely to be female, have lower education, high blood pressure, heart disease, diabetes, be a smoker, and to have MCI.
(Table 1) Low symptoms N ¼ 2430 (81 %) High symptoms569 (19 %) P-value [...] MCI 459 (19.3) 168 (30.3) < 0.001

In models adjusting for age, sex, education, eGFR, and BMI, each 1- SD higher depressive symptom score (≈5.6 points) was associated with higher plasma NfL (β = 0.008, 95 % confidence interval [CI]: 0.003–0.014) and p-tau (β = 0.074, 95 % CI: 0.040–0.108), but not with Aβ42/40 (β = −0.141, 95 % CI: −0.713–0.431) or AD cortical thickness (β = −0.024, 95 % CI: −0.062–0.014).

Additionally, participants with both MCI and high depressive symptoms had lower AD signature cortical thickness (adjusted mean: –0.27, 95 % CI: –0.45 to –0.09), compared to those with no MCI and low symptoms (0.03, 95 % CI: –0.02–0.07), resulting in an SMD of –0.30 (95 % CI: −0.48 to −0.11).

Similar to the main results, severe depressive symptoms were associated with elevated p-tau181—and to a lesser extent NfL—particularly among participants with both MCI and severe depressive symptoms, whereas no consistent associations were observed for Aβ42/40 or cortical thickness across models.

some GDS items overlap with symptoms of MCI, complicating interpretation and underscoring that our findings should be viewed as associations with depressive symptoms rather than clinically defined depression.
